Requirement Statement: The firmware shall specify and use a fixed UART configuration (port, baud rate, data bits, parity, stop bits, and command delimiter) for the command interface so that the listed commands can be reliably exchanged.
Source Text / Evidence:
Command
Action
MOTOR START
Start the open-loop rotation ramp
MOTOR STOP
Disable PWM and stop the motor
DIR CW / DIR CCW
Set rotation direction
FREQ <Hz>
Set electrical frequency
DUTY <%>
Set PWM amplitude within the configured safe limit
STATUS
Report motor state, direction, electrical frequency, PWM duty and driver fault status
Inference Rationale: The PRD defines a UART command interface but does not state the serial settings. Without a defined UART port and framing, the interface cannot be used or verified, and commands may be interpreted incorrectly or not at all.
Acceptance Criteria: With the documented UART settings, a host connects and sends STATUS; a correctly formatted response is received using that configuration.
Preconditions: Target is powered and running firmware.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: UART commands are exchangeable using the documented settings.
Failure Behavior: If UART is configured with different settings than documented, commands shall not be executed and no partial actions shall occur.
Resource Impact: Minimal UART RX/TX buffers and ISR/driver usage.
Comments / Open Questions: Define UART instance/pins, baud rate, data bits, parity, stop bits, and line termination (e.g., CR/LF).

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall reject any unknown UART command with an explicit error response and shall not change motor state or configuration as a result of an unrecognized command.
Source Text / Evidence:
Command
Action
MOTOR START
Start the open-loop rotation ramp
MOTOR STOP
Disable PWM and stop the motor
DIR CW / DIR CCW
Set rotation direction
FREQ <Hz>
Set electrical frequency
DUTY <%>
Set PWM amplitude within the configured safe limit
STATUS
Report motor state, direction, electrical frequency, PWM duty and driver fault status
Inference Rationale: The PRD enumerates valid commands but does not define behavior for invalid inputs. Without defined rejection behavior, typos or noise could put the system into an undefined state, undermining testability and safety of operation.
Acceptance Criteria: Sending an unrecognized command string (e.g., "FOO") elicits an error response, and a subsequent STATUS shows no field has changed from its pre-test values.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: No internal state changes; error reported.
Failure Behavior: On unknown command, do not execute any action; return an error indication.
Resource Impact: Minor code for parser error paths and response formatting.
Comments / Open Questions: Define exact error response format/content for unknown commands.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall validate the FREQ command argument and reject non-numeric, missing, or negative values with an error response; the electrical-frequency setpoint shall remain unchanged on rejection.
Source Text / Evidence:
FREQ <Hz>
Set electrical frequency
Inference Rationale: The interface defines a numeric argument but does not specify handling of invalid inputs. Without validation, malformed values can corrupt internal state or lead to undefined behavior, preventing reliable verification of frequency control.
Acceptance Criteria: Sending "FREQ abc" or "FREQ -1" produces an error response; STATUS before and after shows the same electrical frequency value.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Electrical-frequency setpoint unchanged on invalid input.
Failure Behavior: Reject the command and report error without altering any setpoint.
Comments / Open Questions: Confirm allowed numeric domain (min/max) for valid frequency; define error message format.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall validate the DUTY command argument and reject non-numeric, missing, or negative values with an error response; the PWM duty setting shall remain unchanged on rejection.
Source Text / Evidence:
DUTY <%>
Set PWM amplitude within the configured safe limit
Inference Rationale: The interface defines a numeric argument but does not specify handling of invalid inputs. Without validation, malformed values may set unintended duty behavior or cause parser faults, making the DUTY limit untestable and risking unintended drive.
Acceptance Criteria: Sending "DUTY abc" or "DUTY -5" produces an error response; STATUS before and after shows the same PWM duty value.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: PWM duty remains unchanged on invalid input.
Failure Behavior: Reject the command and report error without altering the duty setting.
Comments / Open Questions: Confirm behavior when DUTY exceeds the configured safe limit (clamp already specified in IF-009); define error message format for invalid inputs.

Requirement Statement: On reset or power-up, the firmware shall hold the motor driver in standby (disabled) via STBY until TIM1/GPIO are fully configured and PWM outputs are in a defined inactive state; only then may the driver be enabled.
Source Text / Evidence:
- STBY shall be controlled correctly to enable and disable the motor driver.
- Motor shall remain stopped after system initialization.
Inference Rationale: The PRD requires the motor to remain stopped after initialization and that STBY be controlled, but does not define the bring-up order. Without holding the driver in standby while PWM/GPIO are configured, output pins can glitch during boot, risking unintended motor movement and violating the stopped-after-init requirement.
Acceptance Criteria: After power-up/reset, STBY remains in the disable state until after TIM1/GPIO configuration completes; scope shows no PWM activity at the driver inputs while STBY is disable. After enabling the driver, the motor remains stopped until a valid MOTOR START is received.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Driver is disabled during initialization; no motor drive occurs until commanded.
Failure Behavior: If driver enable cannot be deferred, the firmware shall keep PWM outputs forced to inactive levels and reject MOTOR START.
Comments / Open Questions: Confirm STBY polarity/levels on X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1; define the exact point at which configuration is considered complete.

Requirement Statement: When PWM is disabled (by MOTOR STOP or driver fault), the three driver input pins shall be driven to the documented inactive level for the factory three-input configuration, ensuring no residual drive is applied to the motor phases.
Source Text / Evidence:
- MOTOR STOP shall immediately disable PWM.
- Use the factory-default X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 three-input configuration.
Inference Rationale: The PRD requires disabling PWM but does not state the required inactive logic levels for the driver inputs. Without defining the inactive state, inputs could float or remain in a state that still sources current, risking unintended torque and making "stop" unverifiable on hardware.
Acceptance Criteria: After MOTOR STOP or while EN/FAULT is active, a scope shows no switching and all three driver input pins at their documented inactive levels; STATUS reports Stopped and fault status as applicable, and the motor does not exhibit holding torque beyond normal driver standby behavior.
Preconditions: PWM previously enabled or ramp in progress.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Driver inputs held at inactive levels; no PWM switching observed.
Failure Behavior: If the inactive level cannot be driven, the firmware shall assert STBY to force the driver into standby.
Comments / Open Questions: Document the inactive logic level for each STSPIN830 input in three-PWM mode per shield wiring; confirm whether additional pull-ups/downs are required.
